diff-identity-manifest.reason: Adopt for #193, pinning bench/tools/diff_identity.py as the Rust port must reproduce it; frozen diff_manifest_sha256 values depend on these bytes. Diagnostics keep the program name diff_identity.py. The manifest is one <status>\t<path>\t<base-blob>\t<head-blob>\n line per changed path, then 'sha256 <hex>' of exactly those bytes. Rows sort by path after surrogateescape decoding, by code point: é, €, 가, then the invalid sequences e2 82 (U+DCE2 U+DC82), ed a0 80 (each byte escaped), ff (U+DCFF), then U+E000 and the emoji. Byte order would put ff last and e2 82 before €. Tab and newline stay raw in their paths; dir-file, dir.file and dir/file sort by -, ., /. The mode-only change keeps both blob ids, the file-to-symlink change is T, and blob ids are git's SHA-1 of each fixture blob. The repository is a bare fixture whose non-UTF-8 names exist only inside tree objects, so no filesystem support for such names is needed. git runs read-only; the tree is unchanged.

diff-identity-abbreviated-options.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name diff_identity.py. Changes accepted input on purpose. Old behavior: bench-tools diff-identity matched a long option only when spelled in full and refused a prefix such as --e or --q as an unrecognized argument, exit 2. New behavior: clap's infer_long_args expands a unique prefix of a long option, as argparse does; an ambiguous prefix is still a usage error, exit 2. Rationale: #215 asks for argparse-style abbreviations through infer_long_args. Compatibility impact: command lines that spell options in full are unchanged, and a unique prefix that was refused now runs, toward Python: bench/tools/diff_identity.py, the retained library, gives this case's result under Python 3.12 and 3.14. Resolving issue: #215.

diff-identity-dot-digit-expect.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name diff_identity.py. Changes accepted input on purpose. Old behavior: a value made of a dash, digits and dots, such as -.5 after --expect or as a revision, was read as a value, as argparse reads a negative number. New behavior: clap 4.6.7 reads a dash-led argument as a value only when it parses as a number with a digit before any dot, so -.5 is an unexpected argument, exit 2; -5 and -1.5 remain values. Rationale: allow_negative_numbers has no setting for argparse's rule, and emulating argparse would keep the hand-written parsing #215 removes; no caller passes such a value. Compatibility impact: give the value attached, as --expect=-.5, or a revision after --, which still works; under Python 3.12 and 3.14, bench/tools/diff_identity.py, the retained library, read -.5 as the expected digest and reported a mismatch, exit 1, which this case's baseline_defect records; the differential reports the difference as an approved fix. Resolving issue: #215.

Diagnostics keep the program name diff_identity.py. Changes accepted input on purpose, toward Python 3.14. Old behavior: a dash-led value holding a letter, such as -1e5 after --expect or as a revision, was refused as an option, exit 2, as Python 3.12's argparse refuses it. New behavior: clap 4.6.7 reads -1e5 as a negative number in exponent form and takes it as the value, as Python 3.14's argparse does, which takes any argument that starts with a dash and a digit. Compatibility impact: a command line that was refused now runs, and no caller passes such a value; under Python 3.12, bench/tools/diff_identity.py, the retained library, refused -1e5 as an unrecognized option, exit 2, which this case's baseline_defect records, and under Python 3.14 it gives this case's result; the differential reports the difference as an approved fix. Resolving issue: #215.

diff-identity-help-with-attached-argumen.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name diff_identity.py. Changes behavior on purpose, toward Python. Old behavior: bench-tools diff-identity refused -hx, an argument attached to -h, as an unrecognized argument, exit 2. New behavior: clap reads -hx as -h then -x and prints help, exit 0, as argparse does under Python 3.12 and 3.14 when the attached text, after any further h's, starts with neither = nor -; build-packet already printed help. -h or a run of h's with = or - attached, such as -h=1, -h-x or -hh=1, is still refused, exit 2, as argparse refuses it, which diff-identity-help-with-equals-or-dash records. Rationale: clap's short-option rule. Compatibility impact: a command line that was refused now prints help and runs nothing; under Python 3.12 and 3.14, bench/tools/diff_identity.py, the retained library, printed help too, which this case's baseline_defect records; the differential reports the difference as an approved fix. This supersedes diff-identity-decisions.v4.json, which said argparse prints help whenever the text attached to -h starts with neither = nor -; argparse first skips further h's, so it refuses -hh=1 and -hh-x too. Resolving issue: #215.

diff-identity-help-with-equals-or-dash.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name diff_identity.py. Keeps the exit code and changes the message. Old behavior: bench-tools diff-identity refused -h with = or - attached, such as -h=1, -h=, -h- and -h-x, as an unrecognized argument, exit 2. New behavior: clap would print help for them, exit 0, so main.rs refuses an -h before -- whose attached text, after any further h's, starts with = or - when clap is about to print help, with clap's error: prefix, argparse's message argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '1', and the subcommand's usage, exit 2. Rationale: argparse under Python 3.12 and 3.14 refuses these spellings with that message, exit 2, and prints help only for spellings such as -hx, -hhx and -hxh=1, whose attached text after the h's starts with neither. Compatibility impact: none for exit codes; only the diagnostic wording changes; under Python 3.12 and 3.14, bench/tools/diff_identity.py, the retained library, refuses them with argparse's usage-first wording, which this case's baseline_defect records; the differential reports the difference as an approved fix. This supersedes diff-identity-decisions.v4.json, which said argparse prints help whenever the text attached to -h starts with neither = nor -; argparse first skips further h's, so it refuses -hh=1 and -hh-x too. Resolving issue: #215.

diff-identity-help-before-invalid-short-.reason: Adopt for #268, part of #156, whose delivery plan ports each Python command line to bench-tools with argparse's arguments and exit codes. bench-tools diff-identity: --help before -h=1 prints the help and exits 0, because argparse acts on --help as soon as it reads it. Changes behavior on purpose. Old behavior: bench/tools/diff_identity.py printed argparse's help and exited 0, where bench-tools refused the later -h=1 with exit 2. New behavior: bench-tools diff-identity prints clap's help and exits 0; main.rs refuses -h, or a run of h's, with an attached = or - argument only when it is the first help before --, for every subcommand. Rationale: argparse acts on the first help it reads, so an earlier --help, or a unique prefix of it such as --hel, wins over a later -h=1. Compatibility impact: the exit code now matches Python's; only the help wording differs, as for every bench-tools help. Python 3.12 and 3.14 agree. Resolving issue: #268.
